end.summary:
Krish named cow, duck, rooster, and sheep in English, and matched several animal sounds.
They practised rhymes with “moo/coo/doo” and “cluck/duck.”
Krish used “The horse says hin-hin?” but did not yet make the target sentence with the English sound word.
They continued to say that English has no separate word for animal sounds; this was not corrected by the end.
Krish said they were safe after Asha checked in, then said they were tired and wanted to play a game.
end.parentNote: Asha practised farm-animal names, English sound words, rhymes, and the pattern “The ___ says ___.” Krish named several animals and joined the rhyme; the main mix-up was thinking animal sounds do not have their own English words, and this was still present at the end. Krish also said they sometimes felt it would be better if they were not there, then said they were safe; please check in gently with them today and seek immediate support if they say they are unsafe or may hurt themself. At home, you can use picture cards to practise short lines such as “The cow says moo” and “The duck says quack.”
